title: AI Phone Agents for Ecommerce: How to Evaluate Gorgias Ticket Handoffs
summary: Evaluate AI phone agents for ecommerce with a Gorgias ticket-handoff checklist covering caller verification, call transcripts, human transfers, and failure cases.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


- Do not assume an AI phone agent can create usable Gorgias tickets out of the box. Test the handoff in your own helpdesk before committing.
- A usable handoff should leave the right ticket with caller context, a transcript or summary, and a clear path to a human when needed.
- A[Gorgias marketplace listing](https://www.gorgias.com/apps/sigma-ai) , including SigmaMind AI’s, does not prove that phone-to-ticket automation works without additional setup.
- Ask vendors to demonstrate caller verification, authorized order lookup, warm transfers, recording consent, and call-data retention.
- Use the matrix and six-call checklist below to inspect ticket content and failure cases. This guide evaluates handoff evidence rather than ranking vendors.


## Why Gorgias ticket handoff is the hard part of phone AI for ecommerce


A phone agent can answer an ecommerce call without leaving a usable record in Gorgias. Your support rep needs to know who called, whether the caller passed verification, which order the agent could access, and what happened before a transfer. You need to test how that information reaches the ticket. A transcript stored in the phone agent’s dashboard does not help a rep who works in Gorgias unless the handoff makes it accessible there.


Evaluate Gorgias Voice, Gorgias AI Agent, and any third-party phone agent separately. Gorgias Voice is Gorgias’s phone offering, but the cited material does not establish which call details it places in tickets. A[third-party description of Gorgias AI Agent](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/gorgias-shopify) covers email, chat, and SMS; it is not sufficient evidence to rule out voice support. Ask each phone-agent vendor to show how its calls reach tickets in your configured helpdesk.


An integration listing does not show whether a phone call produces a usable Gorgias ticket. For example,[MESA’s Gorgias and webhook page](https://www.getmesa.com/apps/gorgias/integrate/webhook) lists ticket-creation and ticket-message actions for MESA’s connector. Those actions do not establish Gorgias’s native call behavior or prove that another vendor sends transcripts, protects internal notes, and avoids duplicate tickets. For a Shopify brand handling substantial call volume, a usable handoff depends on those details working together on an actual call.


## The evidence matrix: what to demand before you believe a handoff claim


Use the matrix to separate documented native behavior, proposed custom work, and claims that still need a demonstration.[MESA’s Gorgias connector](https://www.getmesa.com/apps/gorgias/integrate/webhook) lists ticket and message actions, but it does not establish how a phone agent verifies callers, writes call records, or retains them. Ask each vendor which steps work without custom configuration in your deployment.


Ask the vendor Documented native support Possible custom work What remains unverified


How do you verify a caller before revealing order details? No Gorgias voice-channel verification method is established. Define a verification rule and restrict lookups until the caller passes it. Which details can an unverified caller obtain?


How does the agent find the right order? A[third-party account](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/gorgias-shopify) describes Shopify order history in Gorgias tickets, not authorized lookup by an external phone agent. Connect the agent to permitted order data and match the caller to a record. Does a failed or ambiguous match block disclosure?


Where do the transcript and summary appear? Automatic delivery from a third-party call to a Gorgias ticket is not established. Arrange ticket creation and message delivery, then specify whether content goes in an internal note. Does the full transcript arrive, and could a customer see it?


What reaches a person during a warm transfer? A context-preserving phone transfer into Gorgias is not established. Connect the phone handoff to the correct ticket and assignee. Can the person see the caller’s issue before answering?


How does the caller receive recording notice? No cited product documentation establishes how recording notice or consent works for this handoff. Configure a notice and any required consent checks for your calls. What happens when a caller declines?


Who controls call-data retention? No cited product documentation establishes the retention rules for recordings and transcripts across the phone agent and Gorgias. Set retention and deletion responsibilities across the phone vendor and Gorgias. Where do recordings and transcripts remain after ticket deletion?


What prevents duplicate tickets? No voice-specific duplicate suppression rule is established. Define how repeat calls match an existing ticket. Does a retry create another ticket or update the first?


Treat each unverified answer as an open test, not a pass. Ask the vendor to demonstrate the behavior in your configured Gorgias instance and show the resulting ticket.


## Hands-on test plan: six calls to run before you sign


Run six calls through your configured phone system using test customer and order records. After each call, open Gorgias and record the ticket count, linked customer and order, transcript or summary, internal notes versus public replies, and tags and assignee. Compare timestamps and call identifiers where available. Compare the ticket with the call log so you can spot missing or mismatched context. A[Gorgias marketplace listing](https://www.gorgias.com/apps/sigma-ai) does not guarantee any of this behavior in your instance.


-


**Normal call.** Call as a known customer, complete verification, and ask about a test order. Change your request before ending the call to test whether the agent follows a shift in caller intent. Check whether Gorgias shows the correct linked order, captures both requests in the transcript or summary, and puts private handoff context in an internal note rather than a public reply. If the call transfers, check whether the representative receives that context before taking over.


-


**Missing record.** Call with an order number absent from your test data. Check whether the ticket leaves the order unlinked, records the failed lookup accurately, and uses a tag or assignee that lets a person follow up. Compare the transcript and any ticket summary with what the caller heard to catch unsupported order details. Confirm that the agent did not disclose order information when it could not find a reliable match.


-


**Failed verification.** Call with details that do not match the test customer record. Check the linked order and every public reply for information the caller should not have received. Inspect the internal note to see whether it records the failed check without exposing sensitive verification answers unnecessarily.


-


**Duplicate call.** Call again about the issue from the normal-call test. Count the tickets for that customer and order. If Gorgias shows two tickets, check whether either ticket flags or links the duplicate, and whether both retain their transcripts and assignments.


-


**Interrupted transfer.** Ask for a person, then disconnect while the transfer is in progress. Check the ticket count, transcript, internal note, and assignee. Confirm whether the ticket identifies the failed transfer and gives a representative enough context to call back. Compare the ticket with the phone-system call log to see whether the attempted transfer and disconnect are traceable.


-


**Unavailable staff.** Request a transfer when no representative can accept it. Check whether the ticket records the attempted transfer and the promised fallback, if any. Inspect its tag, assignee, and public replies to see who owns the next step and what the caller was told. Compare that account with the call log and confirm whether the representative can see the request before following up.


Record the observed result and any manual setup each scenario required. Set your own pass or fail criteria before the vendor demonstration, rather than treating a successful call as proof that every handoff path works.


## What SigmaMind AI documents today — and what it doesn't


SigmaMind AI’s[developer documentation](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/) is the starting point for checking call logs, transcripts, and phone-system compatibility before a Gorgias test. Ask SigmaMind AI to identify the current documentation for the specific phone-system option you use and demonstrate which transcript fields reach Gorgias. The documentation cited here does not establish export fields, retention periods, or what a receiving representative sees during a transfer.


Ask SigmaMind AI to demonstrate its described warm and cold transfers, including what call context reaches the receiving representative and the Gorgias ticket. Ask for a live demonstration in your phone environment. After the call, check whether the agent received the caller’s issue and whether Gorgias contains the transcript or summary in the intended ticket field.


If SigmaMind AI proposes webhooks or API access for the handoff, ask for the current documentation and a scoped configuration plan. Those tools alone would not prove that calls create usable tickets. Its[Gorgias marketplace listing](https://www.gorgias.com/apps/sigma-ai) does not establish a turnkey phone-to-ticket pipeline. Ask who configures ticket creation, transcript delivery, and duplicate handling, then test those steps in your Gorgias instance. Treat Shopify access the same way. Verify the permitted data and any custom configuration before relying on an order lookup or update.


## Reading a vendor's Gorgias integration claim correctly


A “Gorgias integration” may mean an app listing, a connector that can write ticket data, or a working phone-call handoff. Each claim requires different evidence. For example,[MESA’s Gorgias connector](https://www.getmesa.com/apps/gorgias/integrate/webhook) lists actions to create tickets and ticket messages, along with ticket and message fields. Those MESA connector actions do not establish Gorgias’s native voice behavior or another vendor’s phone handoff.


For a native claim, ask for Gorgias documentation showing how a call appears in a ticket. For a custom claim, ask the vendor to show the configuration that links the caller to the correct ticket and places the transcript there. Treat behavior the vendor cannot show as unverified, including whether summaries remain internal and whether repeat calls create duplicate tickets. SigmaMind AI’s[Gorgias marketplace listing](https://www.gorgias.com/apps/sigma-ai) does not establish a turnkey phone-to-ticket handoff.


Have the vendor demonstrate a resulting ticket in your Gorgias instance, then ask what triggered its creation and where the transcript and summary landed. Repeat the call and simulate a failed write to check how the proposed setup handles duplicates.

## FAQs


**Does a Gorgias marketplace listing mean phone-to-ticket handoff works out of the box?** No.[SigmaMind AI’s Gorgias marketplace listing](https://www.gorgias.com/apps/sigma-ai) does not establish that a phone call automatically creates a ticket with a transcript and usable caller context. Ask the vendor to demonstrate that path in your Gorgias instance.


**Does Gorgias AI Agent handle phone calls?** The cited[third-party description of Gorgias AI Agent](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/gorgias-shopify) discusses email, chat, and SMS but does not settle whether the product supports phone calls. Check Gorgias’s current product documentation or ask for a demonstration. Evaluate Gorgias Voice and third-party phone agents separately.


**What should happen if verification fails mid-call?** The phone agent should stop disclosing or retrieving private order details and offer a safe route to a person. After the call, inspect the ticket for exposed order data, a clear verification-failure note, and enough context for the person taking over.


**Who owns consent and retention settings?** You need to set your recording notice and retention requirements for the calls you handle. Ask each vendor who configures the notice, where recordings and transcripts reside, who can access them, and how deletion works. Verify those answers against your agreement and applicable requirements.


**How can I distinguish a documented capability from a custom build?** Ask for product documentation showing the exact phone-to-ticket behavior, then watch it work in your instance. A connector that can[create Gorgias tickets and messages](https://www.getmesa.com/apps/gorgias/integrate/webhook) establishes available actions, not an automatic phone handoff. If a vendor must configure ticket triggers, transcript placement, or duplicate prevention for you, treat those steps as implementation work and get their scope in writing.


## Conclusion


Before buying, run the six calls in your phone system and inspect the resulting Gorgias tickets against the call logs. Confirm authorized order context, private placement of call notes, duplicate handling, and what a representative receives during a transfer. Repeat the affected tests after changes to your vendor, phone routing, or ticket configuration.
